fig1_ppv_vs_prevalence.svg: Bayes' theorem turns test accuracy into the positive predictive value P(disease|+). Even a 99%-sensitive, 99%-specific test gives only P(D|+)=0.09 at prevalence 0.001 (purple dot): when the disease is rare most positives are false alarms. A 99.9% test (blue) lifts the curve.
fig2_prior_to_posterior.svg: A defective item B is observed; the partition is three factories with prior output shares P(A_i) and defect likelihoods 0.01/0.02/0.03. The posterior P(A_i|B) is proportional to prior times likelihood, renormalized by the evidence P(B)=0.017, so the dirtiest factory 3 climbs from 0.20 to 0.35 while factory 1 falls from 0.50 to 0.29.
